title: Consolidate lease manager, slim batcher threads, and add KV warmup shim
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Context: Our continuous-batching pipeline and lease bookkeeping have accrued multiple small hot paths and blocking handoffs that increase p99 latency during bursts and complicate KV cache lifecycle. Several hotfixes over the past year introduced ad-hoc threadpools and transient wakers; these are brittle across context switches and make graceful shutdowns flaky.

Problem: - Multiple per-shard lease trackers and ad-hoc timer threads create deadlock windows during rapid shard reassignments.
- The batcher uses a wide general-purpose threadpool that keeps too many ephemeral threads alive, raising contention on the work queue and GC pressure.
- KV cache cold starts are a major contributor to tail-latency for first requests after slot preemption; current priming attempts are scattered and non-uniform.

Proposal: Implement a three-part refactor with low-risk incremental rollout: 1) Consolidate the lease manager into a single, shard-aware lease coordinator with cooperative, non-blocking heartbeats and a consolidated epoch table. This eliminates cross-thread mutex handoffs and centralizes lease metrics. 2) Replace the wide ephemeral batcher threadpool with a slim, bounded worker set and an event-driven task pump (reduces scheduler jitter and allows deterministic shutdown). 3) Introduce a lightweight KV warmup shim: a small, synchronous priming routine that runs as part of slot activation to prefill top-N key prefixes and touch the mmap-backed regions without blocking the main request path.

Trade-offs and constraints: - Centralizing leases reduces duplicate allocations and complexity but adds a single coordination point; must instrument for saturation.
- Slimming threads reduces resource churn but requires careful tuning of worker count per-host and batching windows.
- The KV warmup shim trades a small synchronous cost at activation for large p99 gains on subsequent requests; tuning required to avoid harming slot startup latency for tiny sessions.

Why this is different from previous work: Unlike prior prewarmer efforts, the shim is synchronous during slot activation and intentionally minimal — it does not attempt full prefetch of all keys, only the hottest prefixes identified by recent telemetry. The lease consolidation focuses on eliminating blocking handoffs rather than adding more heartbeat retries or locks.
acceptance_criteria: Lease coordinator replaces per-shard lease trackers on canary rollout hosts with no increase in lease-related errors for 72h
Batcher threadpool reduction yields >=15% reduction in ephemeral thread churn and a measurable drop in GC cycles in staging
KV warmup shim reduces first-request p99 by at least 30% for targeted workload traces in benchmark harness
Observability: new lease_coordinator_* metrics, worker_pool_utilization, and kv_warmup_cost emitted and dashboarded
Feature toggle flags exist for each sub-change and can be turned off without rolling back binaries
implementation_notes: Introduce lease_coordinator module with a lock-free epoch table using atomic epoch counters and sequence fencing
Worker pool: implement bounded async workers with a backpressure-aware queue; prefer reuse over creating threads per burst
KV warmup shim: run top-N prefix touches (configurable, default N=8) on slot activation; metricize time spent and keys touched
Keep clear abstraction boundaries: coordinator only exposes compare-and-swap style promos for lease claims; do not leak shard internals
Add feature flags: ff.lease_coordinator, ff.slim_worker_pool, ff.kv_warmup_shim
Benchmark locally with long-tail synthetic traces and the production trace-replay harness before canary
rollout_plan: Branch + unit tests -> small internal review (ENG runtime owners)
Integration test in staging with canary hosts (10% of staging hosts) for 48h
Canary in production on non-critical region for 24h with incident playbook ready
Ramp to 25%/50%/100% over a week while watching metrics and customer error budget
Fallback plan: disable individual feature flags and monitor for recovery; have image rollback as last resort
test_plan: Unit tests for lease_coordinator correctness under concurrent claims and simulated clock skew
Load tests combining synthetic new-slot activation bursts and steady-state traffic to measure p50/p95/p99
Chaos test: forced shard reassignments during lease handoff to validate coordinator stability
End-to-end regression test to ensure no increase in tail latency for unrelated workloads
Canary monitoring thresholds: lease_retries > 0.5% for 5m, worker_queue_len > 200, kv_warmup_time P95 > 50ms
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: lease coordinator becomes bottleneck -> Mitigation: instrument and partition by host/zone, fallback to per-shard behavior if saturation detected
Risk: slim worker pool reduces throughput for some workloads -> Mitigation: expose pool_size as dynamic config and ramp slowly
Risk: kv warmup leads to longer slot activation -> Mitigation: keep warmup bounded and gate behind feature flag; use sampling for low-latency tenants
notes: Telemetry: correlate kv_warmup_hits with downstream request latency to validate impact
Prior art: reviewed ENG-33109 prewarmer design and decided to avoid heavy async background prefetching
This ticket intentionally keeps changes small per-subsystem to simplify rollback and bisecting
